summary: Packed into just two square miles with nearly 11,000 people per square mile, Valinda is one of the denser unincorporated communities in the San Gabriel Valley — a census-designated place with no city government, sandwiched between West Covina and La Puente along the 10 Freeway corridor. That density shows up not as high-rises but as tightly gridded single-family lots and apartment blocks on flat valley floor, with the San Gabriel Mountains visible to the north on clear days. The home-price-to-income ratio sits around 6.1, which is steep but notably below the broader Los Angeles County average, and rent at roughly $2,050 a month consumes about 25 percent of the median household's gross income — a more manageable ratio than most of the basin. The local economy is overwhelmingly service, logistics, and retail; major employers cluster in adjacent West Covina and the City of Industry warehouse districts, making this firmly a bedroom community with short commutes east along the 10 or 60. With 9.3 hours of daily sunshine and average highs around 77°F, the climate is classic inland San Gabriel Valley — warm, dry, and reliably cloudless, though summer afternoons push well past comfortable. The essential tradeoff is straightforward: relative affordability and freeway access in exchange for a place that functions more as a residential grid between larger cities than as a destination with its own civic center or gathering spaces.
